question.worked_solution:
First, we write the equation $x+3y=12$ in its slope-intercept form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3y & =12 \\ 3y & =-x+12 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{3}x+4\end{aligned}
$$

Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of the new line should be the negative reciprocal of the slope of the given line $y=-\frac{1}{3}x+4.$ The given line has a slope of $-\frac{1}{3},$ so our perpendicular line must have a slope of $3.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=3$ and pass through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(1,-5).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-5) & =3(x-1) \\ y+5 & =3x-3 \\ y & =3x-8\end{aligned}
$$
